cards.method: Textual sentiment pipeline (corpus -> lexicon sentiment -> time aggregation -> elastic-net sparse-regression forecasting)
cards.when: you have time-stamped TEXT (news/reports/tweets) {id,date,texts,+features} and you want to turn it into numeric sentiment indicators and forecast a macro variable: (a) build the corpus, (b) compute the lexicon-based document sentiment, (c) aggregate it over time into several measures (lexicon×feature×time scheme), (d) run a sparse elastic-net regression of y on the measures
cards.when_not: you have no text, only numeric series (-> #219/#220); you want a general sparse regression with no textual sentiment (-> #216/#219); word embeddings or transformer NLP (outside the surface); data ingestion (a file upload — a frontend route, not a node)

alternatives.criterion: the first step: a df {id,date,texts,+numeric features} -> a sento_corpus (a register handle for the chain)
lexicon-based document sentiment with >=1 built-in lexicons (LM_en/HENRY_en/GI_en/FEEL/..) and a within-document weighting
the temporal aggregation of the document sentiment into measure time series; how_time (equal_weight/linear/almon/beta/exponential) — ALL of them are tried -> nmeasures=lexicons×features×time

a sparse elastic-net regression of y on the measures; the alpha and lambda pair is selected by an information criterion (gaussian only), or by out-of-sample cross-validation, which also covers classification

output_key_fields: snt_corpus: corpus (a register raw_handle) + n_documents/date_min/date_max/features/n_features
snt_sentiment: sentiment (a registered raw handle; the per-document records are the chart data) + sentiment_columns (lexicon and feature), lexicons, and how
snt_measures: measures (a register raw_handle) + measures_table (date + the measure columns = chart-data) + measure_names/n_measures/n_dates/dates/dimensions(features,lexicons,time)

snt_model: a coefficients frame {term, coefficient}, with a class column in the multinomial case; alpha and the selected lambda; n_predictors; n_selected, the non-zero ones excluding the intercept; a discarded frame; ic_criterion, blank under cross-validation; fit_dates; and the raw fit as a stub
interpretation_traps: a 4-stage CHAIN: each stage REGISTERS the raw object as a handle (a raw_handle) that feeds the next one; snt_model is TERMINAL
the information criteria (type=BIC/AIC/Cp) apply ONLY to model='gaussian'; binomial/multinomial REQUIRE type='cv' (with train_window/test_window)
y MUST be aligned with the measure dates (length == n_dates); gaussian numeric; binomial 2 values; multinomial >=3 values
how_time and alphas are vectors, and ALL of their entries are tried — they are not a single enumerated choice; a custom weight matrix is not supported
alpha=0=ridge, alpha=1=lasso (the elastic-net mixing); n_selected = the sparse (non-zero) coefficients; a higher lambda => a sparser model
the seed pins the cross-validation fold draw (defence in depth; the information-criterion path is deterministic anyway)
sources: Ardia, Bluteau, Boudt, Borms & Vrontos 2021 JSS 99(2) (computing, aggregating and predicting with textual sentiment)
Ardia, Bluteau & Boudt 2019 'Questioning the news about economic growth: Sparse forecasting using thousands of news-based sentiment values' International Journal of Forecasting 35(4) 1370-1386

Loughran & McDonald 2011 'When Is a Liability Not a Liability? Textual Analysis, Dictionaries, and 10-Ks' Journal of Finance 66(1) 35-65 (the LM lexicon); Henry 2008 (the HENRY lexicon); Stone et al. General Inquirer (the GI lexicon)
Zou & Hastie 2005 JRSS-B 67(2):301-320 (regularization and variable selection via the elastic net); Friedman, Hastie & Tibshirani 2010 JSS 33(1) (regularization paths via coordinate descent)

cards.when: raw text must become a document-term matrix before anything else, and every choice in that pipeline changes downstream results
cards.when_not: the text is already tokenised and vectorised; the corpus is too small for frequency weighting to mean anything

alternatives.criterion: phrases carry meaning single words lose

output_key_fields: dtm: the document-term matrix
vocabulary: the retained terms and the pruning applied
keywords: top terms per document by the chosen weighting
preprocessing: the exact steps applied, for reproducibility
interpretation_traps: THE STOP-WORD LIST AND THE PRUNING THRESHOLDS DETERMINE THE RESULT; a generic English stop-word list removes negations and modal verbs that carry the economic meaning in central-bank text
stemming conflates words with different economic meanings, and lemmatisation is usually the better choice for policy text
TF-IDF weights depend on the corpus, so a document's vector changes when other documents are added
sources: Manning, Raghavan & Schutze 2008, Introduction to Information Retrieval
Gentzkow, Kelly & Taddy 2019 (Journal of Economic Literature 57:535-574)
nltk

cards.method: Topic models: LDA, correlated and dynamic
cards.when: discovering the themes in a large corpus and how they move over time, which no keyword list can do
cards.when_not: the corpus is small or the documents very short, where topics are unstable; you need supervised categories rather than discovered ones

alternatives.criterion: the standard, assumes topics are independent

output_key_fields: topics: term distributions per topic
document_topics: topic shares per document
coherence: topic quality, which is how the topic count is chosen
n_topics: the number used and how it was selected
interpretation_traps: TOPIC LABELS ARE ASSIGNED BY THE ANALYST, not the model; the model returns term distributions, and naming them is interpretation that should be documented
topic solutions are not stable across random seeds, and reporting one run without checking stability is standard practice and standard error
the number of topics is chosen by coherence or perplexity, and these two criteria routinely disagree
sources: Blei, Ng & Jordan 2003 (Journal of Machine Learning Research 3:993-1022)
Blei & Lafferty 2006, Dynamic topic models (ICML 2006:113)
Hansen, McMahon & Prat 2018 (Quarterly Journal of Economics 133:801)
tomotopy

cards.method: Matrix-factorisation topics: NMF and latent semantic analysis
cards.when: a fast, deterministic alternative to probabilistic topic models, which is often more stable on short documents
cards.when_not: you need a generative model with document-level probabilities; the corpus is very large and sparse enough that a probabilistic model scales better

alternatives.criterion: non-negative, parts-based, deterministic given a seed

output_key_fields: components: term loadings per component
document_scores: component scores per document
explained_variance: for the SVD-based method
reconstruction_error: fit of the factorisation
interpretation_traps: LATENT SEMANTIC ANALYSIS PRODUCES NEGATIVE LOADINGS that have no interpretation as topic membership; NMF's non-negativity is what makes its components readable
these methods are deterministic given initialisation but sensitive to it; NMF with random initialisation still needs a seed
component count is chosen by reconstruction error, which decreases monotonically and therefore selects nothing on its own
sources: Lee & Seung 1999 (Nature 401:788-791)
Deerwester, Dumais, Furnas, Landauer & Harshman 1990 (Journal of the American Society for Information Science 41:391)
scikit-learn

cards.when: representing words or documents as vectors so semantic similarity becomes a computable distance
cards.when_not: the corpus is too small to train embeddings; you need interpretable features rather than dense vectors

alternatives.criterion: word-level semantics, trained on your corpus

output_key_fields: embeddings: the trained vectors
similarity: nearest neighbours for queried terms
vocabulary_coverage: share of tokens represented
training_loss: convergence of the training
interpretation_traps: EMBEDDINGS TRAINED ON A SMALL CORPUS ARE MOSTLY NOISE; the vectors will still produce confident-looking nearest neighbours, which is the trap
embeddings encode the associations of the training corpus, including its biases, and those propagate into every downstream use
cosine similarity between vectors trained in separate runs is meaningless without alignment
sources: Mikolov, Chen, Corrado & Dean 2013, Efficient estimation of word representations (arXiv:1301.3781)
Le & Mikolov 2014, Distributed representations of sentences and documents (ICML 2014:1188)
Bojanowski, Grave, Joulin & Mikolov 2017 (Transactions of the ACL 5:135)
gensim

cards.when: constructing an economic-policy-uncertainty or policy-stance index from a keyword rule over a news or statement corpus
cards.when_not: the corpus coverage changes over the period in ways the normalisation cannot absorb

alternatives.criterion: terms carry weights rather than counts
the index is a topic's prevalence over time

output_key_fields: index: the standardised index series
raw_counts: hits before normalisation
normalisation: how article volume was controlled for
term_contributions: which terms drive the index
interpretation_traps: THE INDEX MUST BE NORMALISED BY TOTAL ARTICLE VOLUME, or it measures how much the newspaper published rather than how uncertain the economy was
keyword lists are hand-built and their coverage of a concept changes as language changes; a fixed list drifts in meaning over decades
corpus composition changes -- outlets entering and leaving -- create breaks that look like uncertainty episodes
sources: Baker, Bloom & Davis 2016 (Quarterly Journal of Economics 131:1593-1636)
Apel & Blix Grimaldi 2014 (Journal of Money, Credit and Banking 46:783)

cards.when: scoring text tone with a domain lexicon, which is transparent and reproducible where a trained classifier is neither
cards.when_not: the domain has no suitable lexicon; the text is short and informal where a general-purpose rule-based scorer does better

alternatives.criterion: short informal text, handles intensity and negation

output_key_fields: sentiment: the tone score per document
components: positive, negative, uncertainty and litigious counts
negation_adjusted: scores after negation handling
coverage: share of tokens matched by the lexicon
interpretation_traps: GENERAL-PURPOSE SENTIMENT LEXICONS ARE WRONG FOR FINANCIAL TEXT: words like liability, cost and capital are negative in a general lexicon and neutral in accounting, which is exactly why Loughran-McDonald exists
negation flips meaning and simple counting ignores it -- 'not strong' scores positive without handling
low lexicon coverage means the score rests on a handful of matched tokens
sources: Loughran & McDonald 2011 (Journal of Finance 66:35-65)
Hutto & Gilbert 2014, VADER (ICWSM 2014:216)
vaderSentiment

cards.when: how hard a document is to read is itself a variable -- central-bank communication clarity, disclosure complexity, contract obfuscation
cards.when_not: the text is too short for the indices to be stable; the language is not one the indices were calibrated on
output_key_fields: indices: readability scores per document
lexical: type-token ratio and density
syntactic: sentence length and clause depth
n_words: document length, which several indices depend on
interpretation_traps: READABILITY INDICES ARE CALIBRATED ON GENERAL ENGLISH PROSE and are not meaningful for text dense with numbers, tables or technical terms -- a policy statement's Fog index is not a school grade
the type-token ratio falls mechanically with document length, so comparing documents of different lengths without standardisation is invalid
these indices measure surface features, not comprehensibility; a short-sentence document full of jargon scores as easy
sources: Flesch 1948 (Journal of Applied Psychology 32:221-233)
Gunning 1952, The Technique of Clear Writing
Loughran & McDonald 2014 (Journal of Finance 69:1643)
textstat

arguments.name: df
arguments.description: Handle to a DataFrame {id(char), date(YYYY-MM-DD), texts(char, non-empty)} + optional numeric feature columns (dummies/weights e.g. wsj/wapo). >=1 document.

arguments.name: do_clean
arguments.description: Text cleaning (removal of extra whitespace/HTML/characters) (default False).

arguments.name: lag
arguments.description: Number of time periods in the smoothing window (positive integer; default 1 = no time aggregation).

arguments.name: how_time
arguments.description: One or more time-weighting schemes (ALL are tried; default equal_weight). Valid: equal_weight, linear, almon, beta, exponential ('own' is not supported).

arguments.name: how_docs
arguments.description: Weighting of documents within a period (default equal_weight).

arguments.name: fill
arguments.description: Filling of periods without documents (default zero).

arguments.name: do_ignore_zeros
arguments.description: Ignore zero sentiment values in document weighting (default True).

arguments.name: y
arguments.description: Target (dependent) ALIGNED with the dates of the measures (length == n_dates). gaussian: numeric; binomial: 2 values; multinomial: >=3 values.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: Selection of (alpha,lambda) (default BIC): information criterion BIC/AIC/Cp (gaussian ONLY) or cv=out-of-sample cross-validation (required also for binomial/multinomial; needs train/test_window).

arguments.name: alphas
arguments.description: Elastic-net mixing grid in [0,1] (0=ridge,1=lasso; ALL are tried; default 0,0.5,1).

arguments.name: train_window
arguments.description: type='cv': training window size (positive integer; train+test < n_dates).

arguments.name: seed
arguments.description: Seed before the fit (locks the cv fold-RNG; default 1).

arguments.name: lexicons
arguments.description: One or more built-in lexicons (default LM_en). Valid: LM_en, HENRY_en, GI_en, FEEL_en_tr, GI_fr_tr, LM_fr_tr, HENRY_fr_tr, FEEL_fr, GI_nl_tr, LM_nl_tr, HENRY_nl_tr, FEEL_nl_tr.

arguments.name: how
arguments.description: Within-document word weighting (default proportional): counts=sum of polarities; proportional=/word_count; TFIDF=tf-idf; U/inverseU/exponential=position-in-text.

arguments.name: documents
arguments.description: Documents with an identifier and text column.

arguments.name: stop_words
arguments.description: Stop-word list; omitted = a generic English list.

arguments.name: n_topics
arguments.description: Number of topics; omitted = selected by coherence.

arguments.name: time
arguments.description: Document time index for the dynamic model.

arguments.name: seed
arguments.description: Seed for the random number generator; required for reproducibility.
